newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds higher on interest rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds higher on interest rate hopes.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Wednesday amid continued speculation that interest rates would be lowered as part of an economic package deal, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 106.05
Volume including Makams was 217 million shekels.

"There was stong demand again for unlinked bonds on expectations that there will be an economic programme that will cut interest rates, devalue the shekel and further cut the government budget," said Ilan Doron of Solid Financial Markets.
"Trading in CPI-linked bonds was mixed with a positive trend," he said.
Prices of dollar-linked bonds rose in response to a strengthening of the dollar worldwide and in Israel, Doron said, as well as due to expectations of a shekel devaluation.
On Wednesday, the central bank issued 150 million shekels of dollar-linked bonds instead of the usual 75 shekel million shekels.
"The issue closed very strongly at the market price; it normally closes lower than that. The yield was at 7.0 percent," said a trader.

"The positive atmosphere affected all bonds, especially CPI-linked long bonds, because of the successful issue (on Sunday) of the 15-year bonds," said Danny Alt of Nesuah Trading and Investment. "There is a lot of money in the market."
A 150 million shekel, 15-year CPI-linked Treasury issue was snapped up at high prices on Sunday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
